chunks: From him, from Ayyūb, from Abī Ṭālib, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I said to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: I have estates and dwellings between one village and two villages, at a farsakh, two farsakhs, and three. So he said: Every dwelling among your dwellings that you do not take as a place of residence, then shortened prayer is upon you in it.

key_terms.الْفَرْسَخِ: a unit of travel distance used in legal discussions
key_terms.تَسْتَوْطِنُهُ: you take it as a permanent residence or homeland
key_terms.ضِيَاعًا: estates or landed properties owned by a person

ai.seo_question: When traveling to one’s own property or dwelling, must one perform shortened prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat (prayer) during travel to one’s properties and dwellings. The Imam عليه السلام states that any residence which a person has not adopted as a settled home remains subject to the ruling of shortened prayer when he is there.
